newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila bourse seeks to fill top post in a month.
newsitem.headline: Manila bourse seeks to fill top post in a month.

text.p: The Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) has set a one month deadline to fill its recently-vacated post of president, PSE chairman Wilson Sy said on Thursday.
The bourse's board of governors has agreed to form a five-person search committee to find a replacement to Vitaliano Nanagas, who resigned at the weekend, Sy told reporters after a board meeting.
Three of the committee members are board governors, while the remaining two are members of the exchange, Sy said.
Nanagas abruptly resigned at the weekend following a spate of departures of senior exchange officials triggered by "irreconcilable differences" with the former president, the bourse said.
Sy said many names had been referred to the board as candidates for the post, but he did not disclose details.
Harry Liu, PSE treasurer and board member, indicated the task of finding a new president may be difficult. "It's not easy to get somebody to jump in and take the post," he told reporters.
"We are going to be very careful this time," said Liu, who is part of the search committee.
The wave of resignations at the PSE raised speculation of intense rivalries within the bourse over proposed reforms to make the market more transparent and its members more accountable.

Part of the reform drive included stepped-up investigations of insider trading allegations. Liu said the insider trading issue was not discussed at Thursday's board meeting as it was not on the agenda.
